title: Non-Invasive diagnostics of atrial cardiomyopathy and prevalence of ischemic cerebral embolism in patients with atrial fibrillation
summary:
About 25-30% of the 250,000 strokes occuring each year in Germany are caused by blood clots formed in the left atrium in patients with atrial fibrillation. This blood clots especially occur in patients with a diseased left atrium (so called atrial cardiomyopathy). 
Even more common than a clinically evident stroke are smaller, clinically ,,silent'' strokes that can only be diagnosed in a magnetic resonance imgaing (MRI) scan of the brain. 
Previous studies have demonstrated that an atrial cardiomyopathy can be detected non-invasively by analysis of the 12-lead ECG or by cardiac echocardiography. Therefore, the aim of the current study is to investigate whether a difference in the prevalence of clinically "silent" strokes can be detected non-invasively by ECG and cardiac echocardiogray between patients with and without atrial cardiomyopathy. For this purpose, 935 patients with atrial fibrillation will be included. All patients will subsequently undergo a 12-lead ECG, a cardiac echocardiography, and a cerebral MRI scan. 
In some patients who are sheduled for an ablation therapy for atrial fibrillation, an additional cardiac MRI will be performed to determine the function and structure of the heart. During the ablation procedure, it is also 
possible to quantify diseased atrial areas with electrical disturbances.
We assume that an atrial cardiomyopathy is associated with an at least 10% increased rate of clinically silent strokes. These novel findings might be useful to identify patients with an increased risk of stroke by a cardiac screening and to better protect these patients from stroke by appropriate therapies.
conditions: Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter, unspecified
Stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction

interventions.name: Performance of both a cerebral MRI to diagnose and quantify silent cerebral lesions and a duplex sonography to diagnose cerebrovascular atherosclerosis in atrial fibrillation patients without ACM as assessed by amplified 12-lead-ECG, TTE, cardiac MRI or low-voltage mapping. Assessment

Performance of both a cerebral MRI to diagnose and quantify silent cerebral lesions and a duplex sonography to diagnose cerebrovascular atherosclerosis in atrial fibrillation patients with ACM as assessed by amplified 12-lead-ECG, TTE, cardiac MRI or low-voltage mapping

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Male and female patients aged ≥18 years and <90 years with atrial fibrillation diagnosis 
- Written informed consent for study participation prior to enrollment
Exclusion criteria:
- Prior cardiac surgery or left atrial catheter ablation
- Contra-indications for MRI e.g. claustrophobia, carriage of metal implants, non-MRI conditional cardiac or other devices 
- No sinus rhythm during the hospital stay to perform ECG or transthoracic echocardiography in sinus rhythm
- Short life expectancy due to comorbid conditions
- Heart failure, NYHA 4
- Severe valvular heart disease (mitral or aortic valvulopathy >Grade 2/3)
- Other major disabling disease 
- Acute inflammatory or infectious disease 
- Body mass index (BMI): ≤18.0 and ≥ 36.0 kg/m²
